executive_summary.text: Q3 2026 shows mixed performance across INFANT’s digital channels. Instagram reach and interactions fell sharply versus Q2 2026 but rose sharply versus Q3 2025. Facebook metrics also declined versus the previous quarter but improved versus 2025. LinkedIn activity grew, with higher followers, impressions and clicks, though engagement rate fell. Email campaigns resumed with solid open (60.2%) and click‑to‑open (19.4%) rates. Publications increased year‑on‑year. Data gaps limit deeper analysis of website, KPIs and events.

key_findings.statement: Instagram reach dropped 61.6% from Q2 2026 but was 64.2% higher than Q3 2025.
Facebook interactions fell 59.3% from Q2 2026 while LinkedIn followers rose 32% in the same period.
Email open rate remained strong at 60.2% despite the re‑introduction of campaigns after a zero‑campaign quarter.
Publications increased 72.7% year‑on‑year to 19 items, though open‑access share stayed at 0%.

kpi_analysis.interpretation: Reach on Instagram is markedly lower than the immediate prior quarter, indicating a contraction in audience exposure during Q3 2026.
Facebook interactions declined sharply quarter‑on‑quarter, suggesting reduced engagement on that platform.
LinkedIn impressions grew 19% quarter‑on‑quarter, reflecting expanding visibility on the professional network.
Email open rate of 60.2% is high for the sector, indicating effective list hygiene and content relevance.
Publication count rose 72.7% year‑on‑year, showing increased research output.
LinkedIn engagement rate fell 9.7% quarter‑on‑quarter, hinting at weaker per‑post interaction despite higher reach.

website.summary: Website data not connected; no analysis possible.

social.summary: Instagram metrics fell quarter‑on‑quarter while LinkedIn metrics improved.

findings.statement: Instagram reach and interactions dropped 61.6% and 48.6% respectively versus Q2 2026.
LinkedIn followers (+32%) and impressions (+19%) rose versus Q2 2026.

email.summary: Email activity resumed with strong engagement metrics.

findings.statement: 11 campaigns delivered 1,174 emails with a 60.2% open rate and 19.4% click‑to‑open rate.

media.summary: Press entries appeared for the first time in Q3 2026.

findings.statement: Four media entries were recorded, up from zero in Q2 2026.
19 PubMed items, a 72.7% rise from Q3 2025, though open‑access share is 0%.

events.summary: One Eventbrite event was held, marking a restart after a zero‑event quarter.

findings.statement: Event capacity of 1,100 places was offered for the single event.

conferences.summary: Conference list lacks date information; no period analysis possible.

kpis.summary: KPI tracker lacks date column; cannot segment by quarter.

trends.statement: Across Instagram and Facebook, Q3 2026 shows a downward trend from Q2 2026, while LinkedIn shows an upward trend.

cross_dataset.statement: Increased LinkedIn reach coincides with higher LinkedIn follower growth, suggesting a linked expansion of audience and visibility.

risks.statement: Sharp declines in Instagram and Facebook reach and interactions may reduce overall audience exposure.
LinkedIn engagement rate fell 9.7% quarter‑on‑quarter, indicating possible content relevance issues despite higher reach.

opportunities.statement: Leverage the growth in LinkedIn followers and impressions to amplify research dissemination and stakeholder engagement.
Build on strong email open and click‑to‑open rates to expand newsletter frequency or targeted campaigns.

recommendations.recommendation: Conduct a content audit on Instagram and Facebook to identify factors behind the quarter‑on‑quarter declines and test revised posting strategies.
recommendations.reasoning: Addressing the observed drops could stabilise audience exposure across platforms.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Stabilised or improved reach and interaction metrics.

recommendations.recommendation: Increase LinkedIn posting frequency and experiment with interactive formats to raise the engagement rate back toward prior levels.
recommendations.reasoning: Higher follower and impression numbers provide a larger audience to engage.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Improved engagement per post and stronger stakeholder connections.

recommendations.recommendation: Expand email campaign cadence while maintaining list hygiene to capitalise on the high open and click‑to‑open rates.
recommendations.expected_benefit: Greater dissemination of research updates and event invitations.

best_performing.statement: LinkedIn impressions increased 19% quarter‑on‑quarter, the strongest positive change among measured channels.
